title: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The real number $x$ satisfies $\frac{2x + 23}{2} = 30 + \frac{23}{2}$. What is the linear expression $f = 2x - 23$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $37$. Multiplying by 2 gives $2x = 60$, so $2x - 23 = 60 - 23 = 37$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The linear equation $4(x - 11) + 2(x - 11) = 18$ holds for real $x$. What is the solution $x$ of $f(x) = 18$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $14$. Factoring gives $(4 + 2)(x - 11) = 18 \implies x = 14$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: If $\frac{a}{b} = 2$ and $\frac{c}{b} = 5$, what is the value of $\frac{2a + 3c}{b}$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $19$. Split the numerator: $\frac{2a + 3c}{b} = 2\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) + 3\left(\frac{c}{b}\right) = 2(2) + 3(5) = 4 + 15 = 19$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A line has slope $1$ and passes through the point $(-4, -12)$. What is the $y$-intercept of the line?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $-8$. $y=mx+b \Rightarrow -12=1(-4)+b \Rightarrow b=-8$

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: If $2x + y = 10$ and $x \ge 2$, what is the maximum possible value of $y$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $6$. Express $y$ in terms of $x$: $y = 10 - 2x$. Since the coefficient of $x$ is negative ($-2$), $y$ decreases as $x$ increases. The maximum value of $y$ occurs at the smallest value of $x$, which is $x = 2$: $y = 10 - 2(2) = 6$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, the graphs of $y = 2x + b$ and $y = -3x + 10$ intersect at the point $(2, 4)$. What is the value of $b$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0$. Substituting $(2, 4)$ into $y = 2x + b$: $4 = 2(2) + b \Rightarrow 4 = 4 + b \Rightarrow b = 0$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: If $f(x)=2x^2+x-7$, what is $f(6)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $71$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(6)=2(6)^2+1(6)-7=71$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 71.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: What is the sum of the solutions to $|x - 4| = 2x - 5$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $3$. Case 1: $x - 4 = 2x - 5 \implies x = 1$. Check in original: $|1 - 4| = 3$, right side $2(1) - 5 = -3 \neq 3$, so $x = 1$ is extraneous! Case 2: $x - 4 = -(2x - 5) = -2x + 5 \implies 3x = 9 \implies x = 3$. Check: $|3 - 4| = 1$, right side $2(3) - 5 = 1$. Valid! Only solution is $x = 3$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The absolute value equation $|t - 14| = 10$ has two real roots $t_1$ and $t_2$. What is the sum of roots $p = t_1 + t_2$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $28$. The two solutions are $t_1 = 24$ and $t_2 = 4$, whose sum is $28$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: If $7(x + 2) - 3(x - 1) = 37$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $5$. Distribute the constants: $7x + 14 - 3x + 3 = 37$. Combine like terms: $4x + 17 = 37$. Subtract 17 from both sides: $4x = 20$. Divide by 4: $x = 5$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The point $(4, 14)$ lies on the line $y = kx - 2$ in the $xy$-plane, where $k$ is a constant. What is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $4$. Substitute $x = 4$ and $y = 14$: $14 = 4k - 2 \Rightarrow 4k = 16 \Rightarrow k = 4$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A line passes through the points $(1,12)$ and $(3,16)$. What is its $x$-intercept?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $-5$. Slope $=2$, $y\text{-intercept}=10$. Setting $y=0$: $0=2x+10 \Rightarrow x=-5$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies the inequality $3x - 5 < 16$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $6$. Add 5 to both sides: $3x < 21$. Divide by 3: $x < 7$. The greatest integer strictly less than 7 is 6.

questions.q: If $5(2x - 1) = 35$, what is the value of $2x$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $8$. Divide by 5: $2x - 1 = 7 \implies 2x = 8$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The linear equation $2(t - 15) + 22(t - 15) = 144$ holds for real $t$. What is the solution $t$ of $p(t) = 144$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $21$. Factoring gives $(2 + 22)(t - 15) = 144 \implies t = 21$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The point $A(19, 14)$ lies on the line $fx - 4y = 134$. What is the coefficient $f$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $10$. Substituting $(19, 14)$ gives $19f = 190 \implies f = 10$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In the coordinate plane, consider the lines $p(t) = 3t - 19$ and $q(t) = 41$. What is the intersection coordinate $t$ where $p(t) = q(t)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $20$. Setting $3t - 19 = 41$ yields $3t = 60 \implies t = 20$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Fluency (21–28)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: Which of the following equations represents a horizontal line passing through the point $(3, -5)$?
questions.answer: A horizontal line has slope 0 and an equation of the form $y = c$. Since it passes through $(3, -5)$, the equation is $y = -5$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A line has equation $4x - 6y = 15$. What is the slope of any line perpendicular to this line?
questions.answer: Slope of given line: $6y = 4x - 15 \implies y = \frac{2}{3}x - 2.5 \implies m = \frac{2}{3}$. Perpendicular slope is $-\frac{3}{2}$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(-5)=2(-5)^2+2(-5)-10=30$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 30.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: What is the sum of the solutions to $2x^2-4x-70=0$?
questions.answer: By Vieta's formulas, sum of roots $=-\frac{b}{a}=-\frac{-4}{2}=2$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The height $h$ in feet of a flare launched from a boat after $t$ seconds is given by $h(t) = -16t^2 + 64t + 5$. What is the maximum height, in feet, reached by the flare?
questions.answer: The time of maximum height is at the vertex $t = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{64}{2(-16)} = 2$ seconds. At $t = 2$, $h(2) = -16(4) + 64(2) + 5 = -64 + 128 + 5 = 69$ feet.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: For what value of $k$ does the parabola $y = 2x^2 - 8x + k$ have its vertex on the $x$-axis?
questions.answer: The vertex has $x = -\frac{-8}{2(2)} = 2$. For the vertex to be on the x-axis, $y = 0$ at $x = 2$: $2(2)^2 - 8(2) + k = 0 \implies 8 - 16 + k = 0 \implies k = 8$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The positive variables $M$ and $N$ are inversely proportional such that $N = 85$ when $M = 4$. What is the value of $N(z)$ when $M = 17$?
questions.answer: Since $MN = 340$, when $M = 17$ we have $N = 20$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A certain computer virus infects 5 computers on day 0 and triples the total number of infected computers each subsequent day. Which equation gives the number of infected computers $C(d)$ on day $d$?
questions.answer: Initial value is 5 and growth factor is 3 per day: $C(d) = 5 \cdot 3^d$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: Which value of $x$ satisfies the inequality $-3x + 8 < -7$?
questions.answer: Subtract 8: $-3x < -15$. Divide by $-3$ (reverse the inequality): $x > 5$. Among the choices, only 6 is strictly greater than 5.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A line is parallel to $3x - 4y = 8$ and passes through the point $(4, 1)$. What is the equation of this line?
questions.answer: Slope of $3x - 4y = 8$ is $m = \frac{3}{4}$. Using point-slope form: $y - 1 = \frac{3}{4}(x - 4) \implies y - 1 = \frac{3}{4}x - 3 \implies y = \frac{3}{4}x - 2$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The graph shows the volume of water $V(t)$, in thousands of gallons, remaining in a municipal reservoir $t$ hours after draining begins at a constant rate. According to the linear model, after how many hours will the reservoir be completely empty?
questions.answer: The constant rate of draining is $m = \frac{15 - 24}{5 - 2} = \frac{-9}{3} = -3$ thousand gallons per hour. Using point-slope form with $(2, 24)$: $V(t) - 24 = -3(t - 2) \Rightarrow V(t) = -3t + 30$. The reservoir is completely empty when $V(t) = 0$: $0 = -3t + 30 \Rightarrow 3t = 30 \Rightarrow t = 10$ hours.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola given by $y = 3x^2 - 7x + 12$?
questions.answer: Evaluate at $x = 0$: $y = 3(0)^2 - 7(0) + 12 = 12$. The y-intercept is $(0, 12)$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: For what sum of $x$-values does the graph of $y=x^2-4x+3$ cross the $x$-axis?
questions.answer: The $x$-intercepts are $x=3$ and $x=1$ (from factoring), so their sum is $4$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: If $x^2 - 6x + y^2 - 8y = 0$, what is the maximum possible value of $x$?
questions.answer: Complete squares: $(x - 3)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25$. The circle has center $(3, 4)$ and radius 5. The maximum x-value is $3 + 5 = 8$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A quantity $R_0 = 1200$ increases by $15\%$ to $R_1$ and then decreases by $25\%$ to $R_2$. What is the final quantity $m = R_2$?

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: Simplify $\frac{x^2+12x+32}{(x+8)}$, then evaluate the result at $x=-4$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: What is the quotient and remainder when $2x^2 + 7x + 5$ is divided by $x + 2$?
questions.answer: Perform polynomial division: $2x^2 + 7x + 5 = (x + 2)(2x + 3) - 1$. Quotient is $2x + 3$ and remainder is $-1$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: Which point satisfies the inequality $y < 2x-2$?
questions.answer: Substitute each point; only $(-2, -9)$ makes $y < 2x-2$ true.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: What is the distance between the parallel lines $y = 2x + 4$ and $y = 2x - 6$?
questions.answer: The distance between parallel lines $y = mx + b_1$ and $y = mx + b_2$ is $d = \frac{|b_1 - b_2|}{\sqrt{1 + m^2}} = \frac{|4 - (-6)|}{\sqrt{1 + 2^2}} = \frac{10}{\sqrt{5}} = 2\sqrt{5}$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, the line $y = -\frac{3}{4}x + 6$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $P$ and the $y$-axis at point $Q$. What are the coordinates of the midpoint of segment $PQ$?
questions.answer: At $y = 0$: $0 = -\frac{3}{4}x + 6 \Rightarrow \frac{3}{4}x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 8$, so $P = (8, 0)$. At $x = 0$: $y = 6$, so $Q = (0, 6)$. The midpoint is $\left(\frac{8 + 0}{2}, \frac{0 + 6}{2}\right) = (4, 3)$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The line $L_1$ has equation $2x - 5y = 10$. Line $L_2$ is the reflection of $L_1$ across the line $y = x$. What is the slope of $L_2$?
questions.answer: Reflecting across $y = x$ swaps $x$ and $y$: $2y - 5x = 10 \implies 2y = 5x + 10 \implies y = \frac{5}{2}x + 5$. The slope of $L_2$ is $\frac{5}{2}$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: If $f(x)=2x^2+3x+5$, what is $f(1)$?
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(1)=2(1)^2+3(1)+5=10$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 10.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: An exponential growth model is defined by $p(t) = 9 \cdot 2^{t/1}$. What is the value $p(2)$?
questions.answer: Evaluating at $t = 2$ gives $9 \cdot 2^2 = 36$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: For what value of $c$ does the quadratic equation $3x^2 - 12x + c = 0$ have exactly one real solution?
questions.answer: A quadratic equation has exactly one real solution when its discriminant equals zero: $D = b^2 - 4ac = 0$. Here, $(-12)^2 - 4(3)(c) = 0 \implies 144 - 12c = 0 \implies c = 12$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A rectangle has perimeter 40 and area $A$. What is the maximum possible value of $A$?
questions.answer: Let $l + w = 20 \implies w = 20 - l$. Area $A(l) = l(20 - l) = -l^2 + 20l$. The vertex occurs at $l = 10$. When $l = 10, w = 10$, the maximum area is $10 \times 10 = 100$.
